spans.text: # CP-0 — TDG annual source readiness
Run: `tdg-001`, 2026-11-04. This is a new model-authored response in the current
assistant session, using local file tools. It is not a historical reconstruction,
an isolated provider run or proof of the imported runtime.
Instructions: [CP-0](../../prompts/CP-0.md), SHA-256
Method selection: Deploy V `c4d2e356` ancestry; Deploy Workflow method tree
`6f4a3997e7356352898c410cb7a045722aa5bf03` at selected revision
`2c809379cbba508888b7fbe28ee14eac5a294bbf`; targeted coverage and consumer-readiness
amendments recorded in [the methodology review](../../METHODOLOGY-REVIEW.md).
The linked prompt defines this bounded check, not certification of every CP-0 duty.
## Request
Determine whether the supplied TDG annual PDF can support CP-1 extraction of its
annual primary financial statements and comparative columns. Quarterly analysis,
current covenant compliance, adjusted metrics and a complete credit report are
outside this request.
## Sources
- **S1:** [TDG annual report PDF](../../data/public-corpus/v1/TDG/TDG_FY2024_annual-report_SEC-PDF_0001260221-25-000008_a841225transdigmgroupbookm.pdf).
- Project-root-relative source path:
`data/public-corpus/v1/TDG/TDG_FY2024_annual-report_SEC-PDF_0001260221-25-000008_a841225transdigmgroupbookm.pdf`.
- SHA-256: `dc6a8ea6249e4e919d190a4bbb459d9bf4eded005b7d5680ae911b32d44d44af`.
- Size: 4,378,190 bytes; 160 PDF pages. Page numbers below are **one-based PDF
pages**, not the printed page labels.
- Fresh text extraction: [source-pages.jsonl](source-pages.jsonl), one record per
PDF page, using the project's installed pypdf in layout mode. This is a reading
aid; S1 remains the evidence. No historical model output was used as a source.
- Authority: the document identifies itself as a Form 10-K and includes an audit
opinion. This check establishes its contents, not a fresh SEC download or
authentication. No conflicting version was supplied to this check; versions
outside S1 were not compared. No draft marker was observed on the examined pages.
## Findings
### Identity, periods and presentation
| Finding | Located evidence in S1 |
| Registrant is TransDigm Group Incorporated; document is its FY2024 Form 10-K. | PDF 1: “TransDigm Group Incorporated”; “FORM 10-K”; “For the fiscal year ended September 30, 2024”. |

| Consolidated TD Group and subsidiaries, rather than a standalone subsidiary or guarantor perimeter. | PDF 110: “include the accounts of TD Group and subsidiaries. Intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated.” |
| U.S. GAAP presentation. | PDF 110: “The accompanying consolidated financial statements were prepared in conformity with U.S. GAAP”. |
| Reporting currency is USD. | PDF 55: “Because our consolidated financial statements are presented in U.S. dollars”. |
| Fiscal-year convention ends September 30; FY2024 is October 1, 2023 through September 30, 2024. | PDF 3: “the year ending or ended September 30.”; “October 1, 2023 to September 30, 2024.” |
| Balance sheets are instants at September 30, 2024 and 2023. They do not have duration start dates. | PDF 105: “AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2024 AND 2023”. |

| Income, comprehensive income, changes in stockholders' deficit and cash flows cover FY2024, FY2023 and FY2022. The equity statement also opens at September 30, 2021. | PDF 101 statement index; PDF 106–109 headings and dated rows. The fiscal-year convention on PDF 3 supplies the annual duration starts; the equity opening balance is not a fourth income-statement period. |

| The audit opinion covers the two balance-sheet dates and three fiscal years. | PDF 103: “in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.” The opinion is read as evidence of the document's accounting basis, not a new assurance opinion by this module. |

| Comparative reclassifications are disclosed. | PDF 110: “prior year amounts to conform to the current year presentation, none of which are material.” Use the comparative columns in this filing and retain this qualification. |
### Page map for CP-1
| Content | PDF page(s) | Printed label | Unit / period instruction |
| Fiscal-year convention | 3 | 1 | September 30 year-end; explicit FY2024 start/end. |
| Reporting currency | 55 | 53 | USD, supported by the explicit currency statement above. |
| Financial statement index | 101 | 99 | Resolves statement and note locations. |
| Audit opinion | 103–104 | F-1–F-2 | Opinion text examined on 103; 104 located as continuation. |
| Consolidated balance sheets | 105 | F-3 | “Amounts in millions, except share amounts”; instants 2024-09-30 and 2023-09-30. Preserve embedded per-share par value separately. |

| Consolidated statements of income | 106 | F-4 | “Amounts in millions, except per share amounts”; annual 2024/2023/2022. Monetary rows are USD millions; EPS and dividends per share are USD/share; weighted-average shares are millions of shares. |

## Request

Extract and interpret the annual financial foundation from the sole supplied issuer filing, with complete primary statements, relevant supplemental schedules, explicit gaps and consumer readiness. Scope is TransDigm Group Incorporated and consolidated subsidiaries, FY2022–FY2024, plus the September 30, 2023 and 2024 balance sheet instants. No quarterly, YTD or LTM series is constructed.
## Sources

**S1 — issuer source:** TransDigm Group Incorporated Form 10-K for fiscal year ended September 30, 2024. PDF: `data/public-corpus/v1/TDG/TDG_FY2024_annual-report_SEC-PDF_0001260221-25-000008_a841225transdigmgroupbookm.pdf`; SHA-256 `dc6a8ea6249e4e919d190a4bbb459d9bf4eded005b7d5680ae911b32d44d44af` (matches CP-0). Fresh text aid is `runs/tdg-001/source-pages.jsonl`; PDF pages below are one-based PDF page numbers, not printed labels. Text aid used for statement extraction and note reading; primary statement cells were cross-checked against the page text and PDF images retained by CP-0 for pages 105, 106 and 109. Relevant supplemental PDF pages 45–46 (facility terms, outstanding letters of credit and note maturities), 52–54 (non-GAAP definitions and both EBITDA bridges), 126–133 (debt), 141–142 (segments and EBITDA As Defined), 147–148 (leases), and 137 (tax) were read from the aid; no visual cell audit is claimed for these schedules.

Issuer is TransDigm Group Incorporated. The filing defines “Company” as TD Group with TransDigm Inc. and wholly/majority-owned subsidiaries under control (PDF 3); consolidation policy says statements include TD Group and subsidiaries with intercompany balances/transactions eliminated and uses U.S. GAAP (PDF 110). Currency is USD (PDF 55). FY convention is October 1 through September 30 (PDF 3). Annual income, comprehensive income, equity changes and cash-flow periods cover FY2022, FY2023 and FY2024; balance-sheet dates are September 30, 2023 and September 30, 2024 (PDF 105–109). Monetary statement amounts are USD millions unless noted. EPS/dividend per share are USD per share; weighted-average shares are millions of shares; share counts are individual shares. Balance-sheet amounts are instants, not duration flows.

The audit report states the consolidated financial statements were audited and opines fair presentation in conformity with U.S. GAAP (PDF 103). CP-0 notes that external authenticity/latest-version status was not independently checked and comparative reclassifications to conform to current presentation were disclosed as not material (PDF 110). Source authority is therefore the supplied filed annual report; this module does not authenticate an SEC download.

Subsequent event reviewed: the company drew the remaining $162.5 million available under the trade receivable securitization facility in October 2024 (PDF 131). This is post-period financing and is not added to September 30 reported debt or historical cash. CP-0 G1 about rotated PDF 156 remains unresolved because that supplemental non-GAAP table is outside this extraction; G2 cell/glyph verification remains a limitation for unvisually reviewed pages and notes; G3 external version/authenticity remains unexamined. PDF 156 is not needed for the extracted primary statements or EBITDA As Defined bridge on PDF 142.

Reported net sales rose from 5,429 in FY2022 to 7,940 in FY2024 and income from operations rose from 2,215 to 3,531; source rows are NET SALES and INCOME FROM OPERATIONS on the income statement, PDF 106. The expense block is selling and administrative expenses plus amortization of intangible assets; calculated aggregate expense magnitude is 884, 919 and 1,141 in FY2022–FY2024, respectively, as bridged in Calculations and the transcript. Segment sales span Power & Control, Airframe and Non-aviation; the full channel/category figures and reconciliations are in T4.16, PDF 141. This evidence supports annual growth and mix description, but does not isolate price, volume, acquisition or organic causes.

Net cash provided by operating activities increased from 948 in FY2022 to 2,045 in FY2024, while the FY2024 cash-flow statement reports capital expenditures of (165), acquisition of businesses net of cash acquired of (2,347), and net cash used in investing activities of (2,441); see the correspondingly named rows in T4.5, PDF 109. These reported amounts show that operating cash flow coexisted with acquisition and capital outflows, but do not establish discretionary cash or maintenance needs. FY2024 net cash provided by financing activities was 3,171 and dividends/dividend equivalent payments were (2,038); cash at end of period was 6,261 versus 3,472 in FY2023 (T4.5, those row labels and periods, PDF 109). Dividends payable at September 30, 2024 were 4,216 (T4.6, “Dividends payable,” PDF 105). Declaration, payment and payable balances have different timing and meanings; these figures alone do not establish sustainable distributions or unrestricted liquidity.

EBITDA and EBITDA As Defined are issuer non-GAAP measures; PDF 52 warns against treating them as alternatives to GAAP net income or operating cash flow and cites their limitations. The annual evidence supports historical description, but not current covenant headroom, future refinancing capacity or a forward liquidity conclusion.

spans.text: # CP-2A — TDG static downside screen
## Request

Use the accepted annual handoffs to identify what breaks first under bounded hypothetical annual stresses. This is fresh model analysis and direct use of existing pure calculation functions, not a forecast, full runtime execution or CP-2B event/calendar review. Base period is FY2024, October 1, 2023–September 30, 2024; closing balance amounts are September 30, 2024 instants. Currency and amounts are USD millions. Confidence is Medium, below High.
## Sources
| Input | Handoff evidence and contribution |

| CP-1 | `CP-1-attempt-2.md` SHA-256 `301af0eeed2d90edd2671ef0c71dc759e66c000b3722a0c4ceacfba6fb1332bb`; numerical operands, definitions, source references and limitations. Selected base values: EBITDA As Defined USD 4,173m (T4.10/T4.17, PDF 142); annual cash interest paid magnitude USD 1,158m (T4.5 supplemental cash-interest row, PDF 109); OCF less capex proxy USD 1,880m (T4.10/T4.5); carrying debt USD 24,880m (T4.10/T4.6 classification sum 24,296 + 98 + 486); reported closing cash USD 6,261m (T4.6). |

| CP-1A | `CP-1A-attempt-3.md` SHA-256 `6f63963177c2ea7d54bd043532e250e28625ea70c0ec229d63d55768c2c174fe`; contextual demand/channel, margin/cash conversion and documented debt-supported distribution evidence; critical gaps in current unrestricted cash/liquidity forecast, covenant certificate and executed debt/legal documents constrain inference. |

| CP-2 | `CP-2-attempt-2.md` SHA-256 `249d0cbdf1ba8159dcae68d4ff3241c73ea092ff66353c0c2eef08691e0afa57`; primary downside chain combines aircraft/airline/OEM demand pressure, potentially delayed defense demand, cost non-flex/pass-through, weaker operating cash, distribution/debt-service claims and FY2028–FY2029 refinancing concentration. These mechanisms inform scenario choices, not calibrated magnitudes. |

| Method/code | Selected method `src/deploy_vii/methods/cp2a.md`, imported revision `2c809379cbba508888b7fbe28ee14eac5a294bbf`, SHA-256 `28be81bfb97a83e739e4a514612a2db3bf12b72480128f54c66c33fc2ab06236`. Existing calculation functions in `src/deploy_workflow/owners/cp2a.py`, SHA-256 `b246e5bdcb4622511ac557d4bb3a5afd7aa2f22960f69e00ac4fba235a76b5fe`. Direct BaseOperands adaptation uses actual handoff values and keeps lineage here and in inputs JSON; no fabricated Fact records or source map, runtime, providers or code changes. |
## Findings

**T2B.1 Scenarios — analyst assumptions, not issuer forecasts or probability estimates.** Sizes are purposeful but not economically calibrated. The first isolates CP-2's demand/margin path; the second adds interest cost to reflect the debt-service/refinancing pathway. CP-1A's distribution evidence is contextual to cash allocation risk, not an additional modeled shock.
| Scenario | EBITDA As Defined decline | Cash interest increase | Rationale |
| Base (no stress) | 0% | 0% | Zero-shock control. |
| Demand and margin pressure | 10% | 0% | Illustrative demand/cost pressure from CP-2; CP-1A notes absent price/volume, cost-flex and pass-through data. |
| Demand, margin and interest pressure | 20% | 10% | Illustrative combined operating and interest pressure; the increment is an analyst overlay, not a rate forecast. |

**T2B.2 Base operands.** All flows are FY2024. EBITDA is issuer EBITDA As Defined, a non-GAAP measure, not ordinary EBITDA or operating cash. Interest is positive cash interest paid. “FCF” in the calculator means the OCF-less-capex cash-after-capex proxy, not issuer-defined FCF. Debt is a carrying-value classification sum including separate securitization, not gross principal. Cash is reported closing cash, not established unrestricted cash. Net debt (calculated) is USD 18,619m; it is mechanical and not a liquidity measure.

**T2B.3–T2B.4 Stressed flows and newly calculated ratios.** These are calculated values from the stated operands, not issuer-reported/covenant ratios. Rounded display does not affect exact comparison.

| Case | Stressed EBITDA As Defined (USD m) | Cash interest (USD m) | Cash-after-capex proxy (USD m) | Total carrying debt / EBITDA | Net carrying debt / EBITDA | EBITDA / cash interest | Proxy / carrying debt |
| Demand, margin and interest pressure | 3,338.40 | 1,273.80 | 929.60 | 7.45x | 5.58x | 2.62x | 3.74% |

**T2B.5 Reconciliation.** The zero-shock control exactly retains the supplied E=4,173, I=1,158, proxy=1,880, D=24,880, C=6,261 and derived D−C=18,619 operands. CP-1 does not supply reported total/net leverage, interest coverage or FCF/debt ratios in this accepted handoff; reconciliation to reported ratios is absent. The ratios shown are independently calculated from known operands and do not fill that gap. The later runtime's nine-T4.10-fact offering and reported-ratio gate were not invoked under the specified direct-Markdown adaptation.

**T2B.6–T2B.8 Breakpoints, rank and scenario comparison.** Breakpoint declines hold cash interest at the FY2024 base. Exact fractions control ordering; percentages below are rounded for display. “Crossed” compares each scenario's actual stressed metric, including its stressed interest, to each breakpoint level.
| ID | Break definition or watch | Required EBITDA decline | Order | 10% / 0% | 20% / 10% |
| b03 | 7.0x total carrying-debt / EBITDA analyst watch | 14.8266% | 1 | Not crossed (6.62x) | Crossed (7.45x) |
| b04 | 3.0x EBITDA / cash-interest analyst watch | 16.7505% | 2 | Not crossed (3.24x) | Crossed (2.62x) |
| b01 | Cash-after-capex proxy at/below zero | 45.0515% | 3 | Not crossed (USD 1,462.70m) | Not crossed (USD 929.60m) |
| b02 | EBITDA no longer covers base cash interest (1.0x) | 72.2502% | 4 | Not crossed (3.24x) | Not crossed (2.62x) |

The earliest calculable watch is b03 at a 14.8266% assumed EBITDA decline with interest held at base. This is an analyst watch threshold, not a covenant, default point or probability. Scenario crossings are separate: the combined scenario crosses both chosen watch levels while remaining above zero proxy and above 1.0x interest coverage. Exact outputs, formulas and control checks are in `CP-2A-attempt-1-calculations.txt`.

**T2B.9 Own limitations and coverage.** Debt/cash remain fixed at closing balances; no tax shield or working-capital/capex response is modeled. Assumed EBITDA reduction lowers the cash-after-capex proxy one-for-one. Only incremental interest shock is deducted from that proxy because base OCF already includes base cash interest, tax and working-capital effects. Breakpoints hold interest at base; scenario crossings use actual stressed interest. There is no runway, covenant headroom, funding/refinancing execution, recovery or default analysis. Liquidity, maturities and forward balance-sheet paths remain CP-2D/CP-2G/CP-3C work. Although CP-2B resolves to CP-2A in the catalog, this module does not cover Deploy V CP-2B event-risk/catalyst-calendar duties T5.1–T5.7.

A separately labeled mechanical zero-denominator check (not an issuer scenario) returns interest coverage as not calculable when cash interest is zero; this is recorded in the transcript. CP-1 source limitations remain: PDF 156 supplemental table not reviewed, incomplete visual/glyph verification for some pages, and external authenticity/version comparison not performed. CP-1A's critical executed-document and current liquidity/covenant gaps remain unresolved; price/volume, cost pass-through, acquisition pro forma, maintenance capex and current liquidity are not supplied. Missing evidence is not treated as adverse fact.
## Calculations

See `CP-2A-attempt-1-calculations.txt` for the exact Decimal outputs, rational breakpoint fractions, ranking and crossings, function identities, zero-shock operand validation and separately labeled zero-denominator boundary check. Python execution used `PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python`; no calculation formula was rewritten. Ratios are mechanical newly calculated annual ratios, not reconciled issuer metrics or covenant tests.
## Gaps
| Gap | Effect on this screen / next evidence |
| No reported ratios in accepted CP-1 handoff | T2B.5 reported-ratio reconciliation cannot be performed; no calculated value substitutes for a reported ratio. |

| No current unrestricted-cash schedule, covenant certificate or liquidity forecast (CP-1A Critical) | Closing cash cannot establish available liquidity, headroom, runway or distribution capacity. Obtain current package. |
| Executed debt/indenture/collateral documents not reviewed (CP-1A Critical) | No legal capacity, collateral, priority or creditor-treatment conclusion; CP-4/CP-3C must examine documents. |

| No quantified demand, price/volume, backlog, margin pass-through or working-capital response; no maintenance/growth capex split | Hypothetical operating shocks are not calibrated; proxy is not sustainable FCF. Obtain current operating and capex evidence if sensitivity calibration is needed. |
| No pro forma acquisition earnings/financing bridge; no current maturity/refinancing execution path | No transaction-adjusted leverage or refinancing outcome; forward path remains separate. |

| CP-1 source limitations and CP-1A ownership/control, lender-reporting and related-party gaps | Limits current credit and governance interpretation as carried in CP-2; preserve rather than infer missing facts. |
## Next module

- **CP-2D:** may use the static proxy stress and earliest watch as inputs/questions only; it must add current liquidity, obligations, availability and runway evidence. This screen does not calculate liquidity.
- **CP-2G:** may use the shocked earnings/interest rows as starting sensitivities; it must build a forward debt/cash path from supported dated flows. Closing debt/cash were fixed here.

- **CP-3C:** may use the combined operating/interest mechanism and watch crossings to frame refinancing/LME review. No event-risk calendar, legal terms, current maturity execution or refinancing outcome is established here.

- **Delivery:** may carry the base values, meanings, periods, units, source references, calculated ratios and assumptions with explicit missing-ratio reconciliation and limitations. These are intermediate handoff results; final deliverables must be populated from actual module handoffs and checked against them.

Reference leverage falls from 5.10x to 4.24x; downside from 6.37x to 5.29x under
the same 1,000 annual repayments. This is repayment/growth-dependent and assumes
no extra distributions, M&A, buybacks or financing. It is not an issuer commitment.
The 2-point higher-margin case increases cash generation and strengthens cover,
which is a concrete counterargument to a uniformly adverse conversion thesis.
It wins only if actual earnings convert to accessible cash and cash uses stay
within the stipulated boundary. Missed guidance, lost protection, additional
extraction or unmodelled obligations could reverse that conclusion. No target
date for actual deleveraging or probability is inferred.
